messages.subject: Actionbutton
parts:
I am trying to debug an Actionbutton. It is a part of an R package called rNotebook that builds upon Yihui's Shiny knitr app to provide browser based R Notebooks.

You can run it either by

install_github('rNotebook', 'ramnathv')
viewNotebook()

or

runGitHub('rNotebook', 'ramnathv', subdir = 'inst/notebook')

There is a publish button in the navbar that is intended to publish the rmd source and the html fragment as a gist. Here is the portion of the code.

output$published <- renderText({
    input$publish
    if (input$publish == 0){
      return('Nothing to Publish')
    }
    isolate({
      gist <- createGist(list(
        'index.Rmd' = input$nbSrc, 
        'index.html' = createHTML(input$nbSrc)
      ))
      postGist(gist)
      return('Posted Gist')
    })
  })

Now the trouble is that clicking the publish button does not publish the gist. 

What works is if I click the publish button a couple of times, and then click the Knit button.

This does not make sense to me, since I thought isolate prevents actions from being triggered due to input changes.

My question is how do I rewrite this bit so that clicking publish does the job.

Thanks for all the help in advance.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Actionbutton
parts:
This should work, unless the "published" textOutput is not visible (or it is visible and for some reason Shiny mistakenly thinks it is not visible--we had bugs in this area before, but don't believe we have any bugs in the current master branch on GitHub). But even if it works, I wouldn't say this is the "Shiny way" to do it--renderText blocks should generally be side-effect-free, i.e. the calculation is only interesting in what it returns.

If you are interested in the side effects of the renderText body (which in this case we are--knitting and publishing are side effects, e.g. they aren't reflected in the return value) then in general you do NOT want to put that code in an output. Instead, create an observer:
observe({


  if (input$publish != 0){

isolate({
      gist <- createGist(list(



        'index.Rmd' = input$nbSrc, 



        'index.html' = createHTML(input$nbSrc)



      ))


      postGist(gist)

})


  }
})



The return values of observe blocks are always discarded, so you can't directly use this to indicate whether the operation succeeded or not (for example). However, you can use observer code to set reactive values (basically a hashtable with reactive properties, that you create using reactiveValues()) that are then used to update text outputs.




For much more about observers and reactive values, please see http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview

messages.subject: Re: Actionbutton
parts:
I am facing very weird behaviour. I think it is the interplay between the submit button and the action button that is causing the trouble.

Here are a couple of things I tried.

1. Substituted the observe-isolate code in place of renderText. Publish stopped working altogether.
2. Removed submit type from knit button. Document is knit to html in real time as I type, probably because of the publish button.

My understanding is that the submit button forces actions to be deferred, which is why knitting the document explicitly was required. However, this interefered with the publish button, which is why pressing the action button followed by submit (knit button) resulted in action. Maybe Joe or Winston can throw more light on this.

Thoughts, suggestions....?

Best,
Ramnath
